clue.text: Absurd, like the team that always loses?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: senseless, serving no purpose

definitions.text: like the team that always loses
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a side that never wins ends up without a single point in the table

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading: a losing team has no points.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile or senseless is called pointless, and a side stuck on zero in a league is literally so.

clue.text: Picture — left artist with it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA, Royal Academician, a standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painting described as the artist departing and taking it along.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or photograph of a person, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Poorly in one in very large state

indicators.note: the second in, read as a placing instruction, puts one piece inside another

parts.note: the first in is taken as written
OS, outsize, the clothing label for very large

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly while living in a huge American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is plain letters; the second 'in' puts I inside OS, outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Tired and emotional and shabby

definitions.meaning: first meaning: drunk, the British press euphemism tired and emotional
second meaning: worn and damaged by use

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired and emotional' is a British newspaper euphemism for drunk, and the phrase also means intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both a person the worse after drink and an object worn out by long use.

clue.text: Embarrassed, the Parisian put up church official

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means writing it from the bottom upward

parts.note: embarrassed people go red in the face

explanation.surface: A blushing French official being elevated within the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a lay officer in Presbyterian and other churches.

clue.text: Additional payment made by cleaner entering sweep

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British cleaning lady

explanation.surface: An extra fee charged by a cleaner who comes in to sweep.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a hired cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an extra fee added on top of the normal price.

clue.text: Start of Boléro- unaltered arrangement

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Ravel's Boléro begins with a fixed arrangement repeated without change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' suggests an anagram or a musical setting, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'on a part-time basis', a basis is the footing or arrangement on which something is done.

clue.text: Having completed a circuit, but no further forward?

definitions.text: Having completed a circuit, but no further forward?

parts.words: Having completed a circuit, but no further forward?
parts.note: surface reading: a lap of a track that ends where it began

parts.words: Having completed a circuit, but no further forward?
parts.note: setter's reading: the idiom for having to start over after making no progress, like a board-game counter returned to the start

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes a literal lap, which brings you to your starting place, matching the idiom for wasted effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having to start again from the beginning after an attempt has failed.

clue.text: Careless in dock, arrested by undercover agent

indicators.note: someone arrested is held, so these letters are held inside the others

parts.note: to dock is to cut off, as with a tail

explanation.surface: A careless criminal in the dock, caught by an undercover officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' tempts as a court or harbour but is the verb meaning cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is careless and slapdash.

clue.text: Crime writer wasted year on board

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined and broken up, so the letters are jumbled
on board means aboard a ship, so the ship's abbreviation wraps around the jumbled word

parts.note: SS, steamship, so being on board is being in SS

explanation.surface: A crime novelist who wasted a year aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers was a famous English author of detective fiction.

clue.text: Peacock's last put in to annoy Bohemian poet

indicators.note: something put in is placed inside the other word
the last of a word is its closing letter

explanation.surface: A vain peacock-like display irritating a Bohemian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohemian here means from Bohemia: Rilke was born in Prague.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke, the German-language poet, was born in Prague in Bohemia.

clue.text: Guide showing policeman clergyman's residence

explanation.surface: A guidebook depicting a police officer at the vicar's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a reference book listing names and addresses, so a guide to finding people.

clue.text: Managed to invite endless resentment

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to court is to invite or seek, as in court disaster

explanation.surface: Handling things so as to provoke lingering bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-lasting resentment or ill will.

clue.text: Fiery type, husband associated with Proust novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A passionate husband linked with a novel by Marcel Proust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proust novel' looks like a literary reference, but novel is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotspur, the nickname of Harry Percy in Shakespeare's Henry IV, now means a rash, hot-headed person.

clue.text: Oddity in terribly icy dairy sons may reveal

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly mangled and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange habit on a frozen farm, revealed by the farmer's boys.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar personal habit or quirk.

clue.text: Happy hour — binge in one next door

indicators.note: happy as in merry and tipsy, so the letters are rolled about

explanation.surface: A noisy drinking session in the flat next door.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is a person living in the adjacent house.

clue.text: Duff gen? Vet it for sketch

indicators.note: duff is British slang for broken or useless, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Bad information: check it before it goes into a written piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information; duff means bad or useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a short descriptive sketch or scene.

clue.text: Genuine Greek and Italian film

explanation.surface: An authentic Greek-Italian co-production in cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: True Grit is a 1969 western starring John Wayne, remade in 2010.

clue.text: Gofer may make off with diamonds, jewels originally in our vaults

indicators.note: something that vaults leaps about, so the letters jump into a new order
originally points to the first letter, where the word begins

explanation.surface: A thief making off with diamonds and jewels kept in the vaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaults' reads as strongrooms but is the shuffle signal, meaning leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer runs errands, the typical job of the most junior office worker.

clue.text: Feels upset and annoyed in trading centre in centre of Nassau

indicators.note: in places one word inside another
the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the two middle letters of Nassau

explanation.surface: Someone upset and irritated in a market in the middle of Nassau, the Bahamas capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to feel hurt and resentful, as from a sting.

clue.text: Single and alone

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of a kind
second meaning: without equal, standing on its own

explanation.walkthrough: Both words describe something being the only one of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Unique means the only one, without any equal or like.

clue.text: Rally rounding on head of state

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so these letters enclose the next word

explanation.surface: A political rally converging on the country's leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch, a king or queen, is the head of state in a monarchy.

clue.text: Weird row on street

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece set on another comes after it, so the row follows the street

parts.note: a row or line, as in a mountain range

explanation.surface: An odd argument breaking out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it means a line here; 'on' places it after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd or unusual, a synonym of weird.

clue.text: Build scenery at university

parts.note: a stage set is the scenery
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Constructing stage scenery for a university production.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a student is up at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up is to build or erect something.

clue.text: Game not about to be brought round in place of cheese

indicators.note: brought round means wrapped around the next piece
not marks the letter for about as left out

parts.note: for, as in one swapped for another

explanation.surface: A game moved to the village that makes the famous blue cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place of cheese' looks like the definition, but 'in place of' is wordplay and cheese alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Roquefort is a French blue cheese made from ewe's milk.

clue.text: Water animal and swine beheaded

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a swine, a rotter, a nasty person

explanation.surface: A river creature alongside a pig with its head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine' looks like another animal but means a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a semi-aquatic mammal living in rivers.

clue.text: Guide showing prophet round heart of marketplace

indicators.note: round means surrounding the other letter
the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A soothsayer directing people around a market.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to direct or guide a course.

clue.text: Stand for the Queen over there

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters are flipped to run the other way

explanation.surface: Standing up for the Queen when she is over there.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent is to stand for, symbolise or act on behalf of.
